why does this need to have a `"use client"`? 

I'm NextJS noob but my understanding was that you don't need to put `"use client"` here even though a child component is a client component: [see this page](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components#interleaving-server-and-client-components)

My naive understanding is to add `"use client"` as little as possible, mainly bc:

> Once a file is marked with "use client", all its imports and child components are considered part of the client bundle. This means you don't need to add the directive to every component that is intended for the client.
NIT: I wonder if this could be handled in another way that lets this component be server side (i.e. not "use client"

hey cole! took a look, this component has an interaction that requires it be a client-size component (on hover, the chevron is shown). The animation is a nice touch but it's no big deal if it makes a big diff in performance - what do you think?
